story.head: The Sabres better keep their heads up
paras: The Sabres have won three straight, while the Senators (9-6-1) lost 6-3 to Anaheim on Sunday. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Senators fourth (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Sabres seventh (tied for 15th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.
The Senators’ record (.594) is about what their chances are worth. The Sabres’ record (.607) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.540), largely because they’re 5-3 in one-goal games.

The Senators (2nd) and the Sabres (3rd) both rarely get pinned in their own end. The Sens play slow, tight games (3rd lowest) and get into a lot of chippy games (4th). On the other side, the Sabres don't block many shots (29th). They also get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd), and their knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. The Senators hit a lot, but the Sabres mostly don’t.

Tim Stützle (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 16 GP) leads the Senators in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL. Drake Batherson (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 16 GP) is next in line, with ten points in his last five games. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (10 G / 7 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and eight goals in eleven games against Ottawa since 2023-24. Jack Quinn (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 14 GP) isn’t far behind.
Samuel Ersson (1-3-1 / .866 SV% in 4 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Ottawa, but is expected to start. Colten Ellis (3-1-0 / .880 SV% in 5 GS) is expected to go for Buffalo.
